title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A cryptocurrency trading app displayed false investment gains to a Georgia man through an AI-generated fake website overlay, while scammers diverted his actual deposits. The scammers built trust through a WhatsApp contact, permitting small withdrawals before the victim attempted to access larger sums and discovered the fraud. The manipulation occurred at the point where the victim viewed his account, after he had already transferred money into the system.

This failure involved an AI system deployed in a fraud scheme rather than in legitimate business operations. Detection would have required verification that the investment returns displayed on screen matched actual blockchain transactions and account ledgers, or human review of the account before large withdrawals were processed. It is not established whether the legitimate app itself was compromised or whether the overlay operated entirely outside the app's systems.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a legitimate-looking mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts. Unknown to Jerry, the scammers had created an AI-generated fake website that showed false investment gains on his screen while they stole his money.

The couple discovered the fraud when Jerry tried to make a larger withdrawal and couldn't access the funds. Gwinnett County police confirmed the app itself was real, but scammers had manipulated what Jerry saw using a fake overlay. With their life savings gone, the Dunaways are now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help with expenses, though police say victims in these cases rarely recover their stolen money.
